title: Security services
headline: Stronger protection.|Clearer priorities.
summary: Disconnected controls, excess access, and unclear ownership leave critical services exposed even when security tools are in place. Identify the risks that matter most and turn them into a coordinated protection plan across identities, devices, data, cloud workloads, and AI.
capabilities: Assess critical-service exposure, existing controls, and gaps in detection and response.
Govern human and agent access through lifecycle controls, access reviews, and risk-based policies.
Plan Zero Trust Network Access, secure web gateway controls, and staged replacement of eligible legacy VPN access.
Align device compliance, endpoint protection, and sensitive-data handling with business requirements.
Prioritize cloud and AI risks with accountable owners, response procedures, and evidence requirements.
deliverables: A risk register linking exposures to business impact, affected services, and accountable owners.
A control and detection coverage map showing gaps, dependencies, and licensing considerations.
A phased remediation roadmap with effort estimates, priorities, and acceptance criteria.
An operating model defining control ownership, escalation, exceptions, and review cadence.
outcome: Direct investment toward material risk rather than disconnected tool changes. Establish baselines for critical-gap closure, access exceptions, and response readiness, then use evidence to decide what to improve next.
startingPoint: Start with a security posture assessment.
prepare: Bring your critical services, security inventory, known concerns, and business owners. Agree the assessment boundary and evidence access first; implementation scope and acceptance criteria follow the findings.

title: Threat protection
headline: Reduce exposure.|Strengthen your defense.
summary: Unprotected assets, inconsistent policies, and disconnected threat signals create avoidable exposure. Strengthen prevention and connect investigation through Defender XDR, while addressing cloud-workload protection as a distinct part of the agreed scope.
capabilities: Map critical services to identities, endpoints, email, applications, and protection requirements.
Review onboarding, policy configuration, sensor health, and coverage across supported workloads.
Prioritize exploitable weaknesses and high-risk configurations using business impact and exposure.
Connect related signals to investigation workflows with clear containment and escalation decisions.
Pilot hardening changes with operational owners, user-impact assessment, and rollback criteria.
deliverables: An asset-to-protection coverage map identifying unmanaged, unsupported, or partially protected systems.
A risk-ranked hardening backlog with remediation owners, dependencies, and verification steps.
A protection design documenting policy intent, exceptions, and required product capabilities.
A phased rollout plan with pilot acceptance, change approvals, and operational handover.
outcome: Reduce uncertainty about what is protected and which gaps deserve attention first. Track coverage, critical exposure, exception age, and verified remediation against an agreed baseline; protection does not eliminate all risk.
startingPoint: Start with a threat-protection readiness review.
prepare: Bring critical services, protection reports, known exposure, and change windows. Start with a bounded assessment or hardening pilot. Active incident response and specialist operational-technology assessment are separate scopes.

title: Data security
headline: Know your information.|Protect how it is used.
summary: Overshared documents, unclear ownership, and inconsistent handling make sensitive information difficult to protect. Establish practical data boundaries that support collaboration and AI adoption without treating every document or business process the same.
capabilities: Identify sensitive repositories, accountable owners, excess access, and external-sharing patterns.
Define classifications and sensitivity labels around business handling needs and user workflows.
Design supported data loss prevention policies, starting with observation and controlled enforcement.
Align retention, audit, investigation, and insider-risk requirements with legal and privacy owners.
Review how assistants access protected information and where workload-specific controls differ.
deliverables: A repository risk assessment identifying priority data, exposure paths, and remediation owners.
A classification and handling model with label definitions, examples, and ownership.
A policy rollout plan covering test cases, user impact, exceptions, and enforcement gates.
A control-to-evidence matrix and operating procedures for reviews, investigations, and policy changes.
outcome: Make protection decisions explainable and reduce avoidable oversharing. Measure classification coverage, excess access, policy effectiveness, and exception resolution while maintaining agreed collaboration needs. Configuration supports compliance processes; it does not establish compliance by itself.
startingPoint: Start with a data protection and readiness assessment.
prepare: Bring priority repositories, information owners, sharing patterns, and applicable obligations. Begin with a representative data scope and policy pilot; confirm legal, privacy, and licensing requirements before enforcement.

title: Modern security operations
headline: Connect the signals.|Operationalize the response.
summary: Alert volume is not the same as threat coverage. When signals lack context and response ownership is unclear, important incidents compete with noise. Build a security operating model that connects relevant telemetry, useful detections, and accountable action.
capabilities: Assess triage, investigation, escalation, and handoffs against priority business threats.
Select Sentinel data sources with explicit coverage, ingestion-cost, and retention requirements.
Engineer and tune detections using Defender XDR context and representative investigation scenarios.
Pilot Security Copilot for evidence summaries and investigation assistance, with analyst validation and scoped access.
Design response automation with approval gates for disruptive actions and recoverable failure paths.
Exercise runbooks, capture lessons, and establish a recurring detection-improvement process.
deliverables: A threat-coverage and operating-model assessment identifying gaps, bottlenecks, and ownership.
A prioritized detection backlog with data dependencies, tuning criteria, and validation scenarios.
Investigation and response runbooks with evidence requirements, escalation paths, and approvals.
An operations handover and scorecard covering alert quality, investigation time, and detection health.
outcome: Help analysts spend effort on actionable incidents and make response decisions more consistent. Establish baselines for investigation quality, escalation timeliness, and detection gaps before setting service-improvement targets.
startingPoint: Start with a security operations modernization roadmap.
prepare: Bring data-source inventories, recurring alert examples, current workflows, and operational constraints. Start with priority detection scenarios. Monitoring hours, incident response, and service targets require a separate explicit agreement.

title: AI Business Solutions
headline: Better ways to work.|A clearer case for AI.
summary: Repeated tasks, fragmented knowledge, and disconnected handoffs slow teams down. Identify where better collaboration, simpler processes, and useful AI can improve everyday work, then build the business case and adoption path before expanding investment.
capabilities: Improve modern work productivity through Microsoft 365 collaboration, content ownership, and Viva employee experience.
Prioritize role-based Copilot and agent use cases around real tasks and approved information.
Redesign business processes before automating decisions, approvals, and system handoffs.
Design custom AI with bounded access, representative evaluation, and accountable operational owners.
Equip users and managers with role-based learning, support, and privacy-aware adoption measures.
deliverables: A ranked opportunity portfolio comparing business value, feasibility, readiness, and change effort.
A current-state assessment and future-state blueprint for the selected workplace or process scope.
A pilot charter with baseline measures, success criteria, controls, and expansion decisions.
An adoption and delivery roadmap with training, support responsibilities, and ownership.
outcome: Focus investment on useful work improvements rather than isolated tool rollout. Measure task quality, process friction, and sustained adoption alongside the cost of change; usage alone is not evidence of financial return.
startingPoint: Start with an AI strategy and governance roadmap.
prepare: Bring a recurring business problem, its owner, and representative tasks. Choose one workplace, process, or AI opportunity and agree the evidence needed to proceed, reshape, or stop the pilot.

title: Copilot readiness and adoption
headline: Prepare the foundation.|Make adoption useful.
summary: Licenses alone do not make Copilot useful. Poor information access, weak task selection, and limited user support can undermine adoption. Prepare Microsoft 365 Copilot around representative roles, trusted content, and clear expectations for reviewing results.
capabilities: Select role-based tasks where drafting, discovery, or analysis can address a recurring work problem.
Review licensing, identity, device, application, and information-access prerequisites.
Identify oversharing, stale content, and protection gaps that affect permission-aware responses.
Design practical learning, manager support, feedback collection, and issue escalation.
Evaluate output quality and task usefulness with representative users before widening access.
deliverables: A role-and-task opportunity map with baseline effort, quality expectations, and content dependencies.
A readiness report and ranked remediation backlog with accountable owners.
A pilot charter defining participants, safeguards, evaluation tasks, and proceed-or-stop criteria.
An enablement playbook with learning scenarios, support routes, and privacy-aware adoption measures.
outcome: Make expansion decisions using evidence of useful, responsible work rather than license activation. Compare output quality, correction effort, user confidence, and sustained adoption; any savings depend on validated changes to actual work.
startingPoint: Start with a focused Copilot readiness engagement.
prepare: Bring pilot roles, sample tasks, approved knowledge sources, and relevant policies. Agree the pilot boundary and remediation priorities first, then confirm current licensing and supported capabilities before rollout.

title: Business process transformation
headline: Reduce the handoffs.|Keep decisions accountable.
summary: Manual re-entry, approval queues, and unclear handoffs create delays and rework. Redesign the process before adding automation, connecting records and decisions around a business outcome with explicit ownership for exceptions and consequential actions.
capabilities: Map current work, wait times, duplicate entry, and the causes of recurring exceptions.
Design a simpler future-state flow across sales, service, finance, or operations.
Connect approved business and collaboration systems with deliberate data ownership and access.
Define human decisions, automated actions, approval thresholds, and recovery from failed steps.
Plan representative acceptance tests, user adoption, release controls, and support handover.
deliverables: A current-state process map and baseline showing bottlenecks, handoffs, and rework drivers.
A future-state design with decision rights, approvals, and exception-routing rules.
An integration blueprint and prioritized implementation backlog with system dependencies.
Acceptance scenarios and operating runbooks covering failures, duplicate actions, and escalation.
outcome: Create a process people can operate and improve, not just an automated sequence. Track cycle time, first-time quality, exception volume, and service outcomes against the baseline while retaining required approvals and auditability.
startingPoint: Start with one important process and its business owner.
prepare: Start with one important process and its accountable owner. Bring sample cases, systems, volumes, and common exceptions. Financial, contractual, and externally consequential actions require explicit authorization and agreed controls.

title: Custom AI solutions and governance
headline: Use your knowledge.|Bound the capability.
summary: Generic assistants may not understand your business context or safely execute the work you need. Design a focused assistant or agent around approved knowledge, bounded tools, and measurable task quality, with governance built into the delivery approach.
capabilities: Assess task feasibility, business ownership, source quality, and permitted data use.
Design permission-aware knowledge retrieval, source references, and handling of uncertain answers.
Connect approved tools and Model Context Protocol servers with scoped permissions and action approvals.
Test representative tasks, denied access, misleading inputs, and safe failure behavior.
Define release decisions, human escalation, monitoring, change review, and retirement.
deliverables: A solution blueprint defining task boundaries, knowledge sources, permissions, and decision ownership.
A scoped prototype demonstrating the agreed workflow and integration boundaries.
An evaluation dataset and results report covering task quality, groundedness, and failure cases.
A production-readiness backlog with release gates, monitoring requirements, and support ownership.
outcome: Establish whether a custom agent solves a real problem well enough to justify further investment. Measure task success, unsupported answers, safe failure, latency, and cost per useful interaction rather than relying on a polished prototype.
startingPoint: Start with a scoped use case and clear boundaries.
prepare: Bring representative tasks, approved information, an accountable owner, and intended integrations. Start with a bounded prototype; production deployment and expanded permissions require separate readiness and authorization decisions.

title: Cloud and AI Platforms
headline: Modernize with purpose.|Innovate on solid ground.
summary: Aging applications, fragmented data, and unpredictable costs make change harder than it needs to be. Establish cloud, data, and AI foundations around business priorities, with deliberate decisions about reliability, security, ownership, and ongoing operations.
capabilities: Design governed Azure foundations with identity, networking, policy, and Defender for Cloud posture and protection planning.
Assess application dependencies and prioritize retention, migration, or modernization decisions.
Connect data integration, shared definitions, quality, and access into trusted analytical foundations.
Plan AI application hosting, evaluation, integrations, and release controls.
Build recovery, monitoring, support, and cost accountability into the operating model.
deliverables: A landscape assessment linking platform constraints and technical debt to business priorities.
A target architecture with documented tradeoffs, dependencies, and responsibility boundaries.
A sequenced delivery roadmap with workload priorities, readiness gates, and effort estimates.
An operations plan covering recovery objectives, monitoring, cost ownership, and improvement reviews.
outcome: Create a foundation that supports change without transferring hidden risk into operations. Baseline reliability, recovery, data quality, and cost allocation, then use those measures to prioritize modernization and investment.
startingPoint: Start with a cloud and data modernization roadmap.
prepare: Bring the application landscape, critical data sources, current costs, and operating constraints. Select a bounded platform or workload scope and agree the decisions the roadmap must enable.

title: Cloud modernization
headline: Move the business forward.|Not just the workload.
summary: Moving workloads without understanding dependencies can carry technical debt and operational risk into the cloud. Decide what to retain, retire, migrate, or redesign, then sequence change around business continuity and a governed Azure foundation.
capabilities: Discover workloads, dependencies, support constraints, and business criticality.
Assess disposition options against compatibility, risk, operating cost, and business value.
Design landing-zone identity, connectivity, policy, and workload responsibility boundaries.
Plan Defender for Cloud coverage alongside performance, recovery, and data residency requirements.
Plan migration waves, representative pilots, cutover decisions, rollback, and support transition.
deliverables: A workload inventory and dependency map with disposition recommendations and decision rationale.
A target architecture documenting platform controls, connectivity, and operational responsibilities.
A wave plan with prerequisites, risk treatment, effort estimates, and business change windows.
Cutover and acceptance criteria covering recovery tests, performance, support readiness, and rollback.
outcome: Make modernization decisions with a clearer view of cost, dependencies, and service risk. Track readiness, migration exceptions, validated recovery, and operating performance against the baseline before retiring legacy capacity.
startingPoint: Start with a bounded portfolio or platform assessment.
prepare: Bring workload owners, architecture records, utilization data, and change windows. Start with a bounded portfolio or pilot wave; validate licensing, regional availability, and data residency before committing to migration.

title: Governed data and analytics
headline: Connect the information.|Preserve its meaning.
summary: Conflicting reports and disconnected data force teams to reconcile numbers before making decisions. Build governed data products with shared meaning, reliable pipelines, and accountable ownership so analytics and AI use information people can trust.
capabilities: Trace priority business questions to source systems, data owners, and integration constraints.
Design lakehouse, warehouse, and semantic models around agreed analytical needs.
Define quality rules, freshness expectations, lineage, classification, and access boundaries.
Deliver a bounded reporting or analytical pilot with business validation of key measures.
Establish pipeline monitoring, issue resolution, change control, and data-product ownership.
deliverables: A source-to-consumption blueprint showing integration paths, responsibilities, and dependencies.
A prioritized data-product backlog with shared metric definitions and business acceptance criteria.
A quality and access control plan with exception handling and traceable evidence.
A reporting pilot and operating model covering refresh failures, ownership, and change approval.
outcome: Reduce the uncertainty behind reports and create a reusable basis for decisions. Measure freshness, reconciliation effort, quality exceptions, and consistency of key measures rather than treating data consolidation alone as success.
startingPoint: Start with a business question and the data it needs.
prepare: Start with one important business question and the data it needs. Bring current reports, source owners, and known quality issues. Confirm permitted reuse, privacy requirements, and access before integrating sources.

title: AI application platforms
headline: Make innovation deployable.|Make it operable.
summary: A successful AI prototype can still lack the controls needed for a dependable service. Establish a deployable platform for models, knowledge, and tools with explicit evaluation, release, monitoring, and cost responsibilities before production use.
capabilities: Select hosting and supported model options against quality, latency, region, and cost requirements.
Design identity, secrets handling, knowledge access, and approved Model Context Protocol integrations.
Define orchestration boundaries, workflow handoffs, retries, and human escalation paths.
Create representative evaluations and release gates for quality, access controls, and failure behavior.
Use GitHub Copilot for development assistance with human code review and tests.
Plan budgets, monitoring, recovery, version changes, and accountable support.
deliverables: A reference architecture with hosting choices, trust boundaries, and documented tradeoffs.
A scoped platform foundation with environment configuration and repeatable deployment steps.
An evaluation and release plan with test datasets, acceptance thresholds, and rollback criteria.
An operations runbook covering monitoring, cost alerts, incidents, and model or application changes.
outcome: Make the transition from prototype to operation a deliberate engineering decision. Baseline task quality, security findings, latency, availability objectives, and cost per useful task; release only when agreed readiness criteria are met.
startingPoint: Start with a use case and a production-readiness review.
prepare: Bring a representative application, data and model requirements, intended integrations, and operating constraints. Agree the platform boundary and pilot workload; production readiness remains separate from prototype performance.
